derivedTables.displayId: Heritage spending before and after the pandemic

derive.code:
import pandas as pd
d=pd.read_parquet('data/sdg11_national.parquet')
x=d[d.indicator_id.eq('HEXPCSTPPPCAP.HER.PU')]
a=x[x.year.between(2017,2019)].sort_values('year').groupby('COUNTRY_ID').tail(1)
b=x[x.year.between(2022,2024)].sort_values('year').groupby('COUNTRY_ID').tail(1)
out=a.merge(b,on='COUNTRY_ID',suffixes=('_before','_after'))
out['change_percent']=100*(out.value_after/out.value_before-1)
out['direction']=out.change_percent.map(lambda v:'Higher than before the pandemic' if v>0 else 'Lower than before the pandemic' if v<0 else 'Unchanged')
out['countries']=1

concepts.explanation: Uses each country's latest available value in 2017–2019 as the baseline and its latest available value in 2022–2024 as the comparison: `change_percent = 100 * (value_after / value_before - 1)`.
`direction = 'Higher than before the pandemic' if change_percent > 0; 'Lower than before the pandemic' if change_percent < 0; otherwise 'Unchanged'`.

codeExecutions.code:
import pandas as pd
ind=pd.read_parquet('data/sdg11_indicators.parquet'); print(ind.to_string(index=False))
d=pd.read_parquet('data/sdg11_national.parquet'); s=pd.read_parquet('data/sdg11_sources.parquet')
k=ind.loc[ind.indicator.str.startswith('Total public expenditure per capita spent'),'indicator_id'].iloc[0]
x=d[d.indicator_id.eq(k)]; print('YEARS',x.groupby('year').size())
a=x[x.year.between(2017,2019)].sort_values('year').groupby('COUNTRY_ID').tail(1); b=x[x.year.between(2022,2024)].sort_values('year').groupby('COUNTRY_ID').tail(1)
m=a.merge(b,on='COUNTRY_ID',suffixes=('_before','_after')); m['change']=100*(m.value_after/m.value_before-1)
print(m[['COUNTRY_ID','country_after','year_before','value_before','year_after','value_after','change']].to_string(index=False)); print('notes',s[s.indicator_id.eq(k)].to_string(index=False))

textTurns.content:
**Slightly more often than not—but there is no clear worldwide rise.** Among 31 countries with figures before the pandemic and in 2022–2024, 17 reported higher public heritage spending per person and 14 reported lower spending. The middle country’s change was about **+4%**, after adjusting for inflation.

This compares each country’s latest 2022–2024 figure with its latest 2017–2019 figure and includes both cultural and natural heritage, not private spending.

Coverage is limited and reporting differs between countries; Moldova also changed its methodology, so these figures cannot establish a global spending trend.
